18.t: Working with data: smoking and birth mass
q: State the mean birth mass for non-smokers.
Calculate the difference between non-smokers and over 20 per day.
Explain how smoking can reduce a baby’s growth.
Carbon monoxide reduces the oxygen the blood carries, and nicotine narrows blood vessels, so less oxygen and food cross the placenta.
The y-axis starts at 2.5 kg. Explain how this could mislead a reader.
The bars look very different in height, making the effect look bigger than it is (the drop is about 12%). Always check the axis scale.
